correctness.rationale: Exact neighbor-count inequalities for all three layers give four feasibility cases by middle occupancy. Every inclusion-minimal case b=0,1,2,3,4 and nonexistence for b>=5 is proved by single-vertex deletion. Six disjoint contribution counts give the polynomial. The original-predicate verifier exhaustively checked all 2,396,672 subsets for n=3..7, and full structural and coefficient equality for n=6,7. The infinite theorem is supported by the proof, not the experiments.

originality.rationale: The nearest primary theorems of Kazemi–Pahlavsay–Stones (2015), Carballosa–Wisby (2020) and Li–Yue–Zhang (2023) address scalar minima on rook graphs or products of paths, not deletion-minimal double-total domination of K_n Cartesian P_3. The known scalar lower bound six is expressly not claimed original. Indexed semantic searches with predicate aliases and graph descriptions found no same-polynomial implication. Unindexed and differently formulated prior results remain an acknowledged priority risk.
residual_risks: Indexed searches and inspected primary papers cannot rule out all other or unpublished statements.

The 2023 motivating product-of-paths paper was searched and sampled across theorem/conclusion sections rather than independently re-derived; it is not asserted to be a complete proof of global publication priority.

value.rationale: The polynomial classifies every deletion-irredundant two-neighbor monitoring configuration on a natural connected family, not just minimum cardinality. For n>=8 it has a sparse, noninterval support {6,7,8,9,n+2,2n}; the unique largest minimal configuration uses both outer layers and lies 2n-6 above the minimum. This distinguishes reliably irredundant protection configurations from ordinary optimization and creates an exact benchmark for deletion-based heuristics. It does not rely on unproved downstream consequences.
